original: Like a fairy tale
It's a sign the story has reached its end
Like a single passage taken from
A journey that was too long
Of the evil that once cast a shadow
Across this land
And the memories of the short journey
With the hero who defeated it
The story ends
And the hero goes to sleep
Leaving this land with
Days of peace and quiet
The passage of time heartlessly
Makes people forget
Even the tracks left behind by his life
Begin to rust
Just the same
Your words and wishes and courage
Are still inside of me
And they live on
We chose the same path
That's all it was supposed to be
Why is it that at some point
I wanted to understand the reason for
The tears that fall down my cheeks
Even now
If I retrace the journey we walked together
Even though you're not there
I know I'll be able to find it
I see.
I remember now.
It was Frieren.

The mage who contributed significantly
to humanity's analysis of Zoltraak

and slew more demons
than anyone else in history.
Frieren the Slayer.
One of the geniuses I despise.
You'll have to rest for a while.
Thank you.
Hey!
Are you okay?
Because of you, I'll survive.
You have my thanks.
I'll pardon your mage companion as well.
She was right.
Now Frieren can return to town.

Let's have her defeat Lügner
and the other demon.
Ms. Frieren didn't kill the guard.
I know. The demons did it.

More importantly,
that mage's name is Frieren?
Yes.
The elven mage who adventured with the Hero?
Then I've committed a grave discourtesy.

The Granat family owes the
party of heroes a debt.

When this town was attacked by demons
during my grandfather's rule,
they were the ones who drove them off.
They faced the same enemy as we do now.

It was Aura, one of the
Seven Sages of Destruction.
It's been a while, Aura.
Indeed, Frieren. About eighty years, I'd say.

You're heading to the town
up ahead, aren't you?
I'd appreciate it if you turned back.
No.
Why not?
Because I have an overwhelming advantage.
Oh?
You have more puppets than before.

Demon magic must be unbelievably
powerful to control this many.

Humanity's magic could never
dream of reaching such heights.
But your magic couldn't be more disgusting.
It makes me want to puke.
That's not a nice thing to say.
It took a lot of work to gather this many.
I recognize some of those suits of armor.

Aura, it seems I must
kill you here after all.
The Scales of Obedience.

It's the reason we haven't been able
to defeat Aura in all these years.

Her magic allows her to force
others to obey her will.
The magics of the Seven Sages of Destruction
are beyond human knowledge and reason.

Aura places her own soul
and that of her target on the scales

and weighs the magnitude of
their mana against each other.

The one with greater mana
gains control of the other,

turning them into a puppet for all eternity—
until their body withers to dust.

It's a risky spell, but that's
what makes it powerful.

And in the hands of someone with mana
as tremendous as Aura, it's unbeatable.
Is there no way to counter it?

Though the weight of Aura's mana
is enough to fully tip the scales,
the scales themselves do judge fairly.

If a soul with greater mana than Aura's
were to be placed on the scales,
Aura could be defeated.

But they say that hasn't happened
once in the five hundred years
since Aura became a Sage of Destruction.
Then there's no way to fight it?
There was.

Those with powerful wills could
temporarily resist the spell.

The greater the individual,
the more iron their will.
And even then, it was only temporary?
But it was a fatal flaw.

The strong-willed must have been
an obstacle to her.
So...

Aura the Guillotine dealt with them in the
most logical way after gaining control.
It's a tragic tale.

Well? My immortal army
is powerful, isn't it?
I'm surprised.
You dispelled the magic I'd cast on them.
No one's ever done that before.

Such powerful dispelling magic must expend
a considerable amount of mana.
Why would you use such a roundabout method?

The last time we fought, you blew them away
with flashy spells left and right.
Himmel scolded me afterward.

Then that's all the more reason
not to do this.
Why?
Himmel is long gone, isn't he?
I see. Good.
You demons are monsters after all.
I can kill you without mercy.
Okay.
I've regained most of my mobility.
Father, this place is safe, right?

Yes. It's not as strong as the
town's defensive barrier,
but there is a barrier around this church.
Then wait here, Graf.
Brat, what do you plan to do?

Do you think the demons will just leave
if we all hole up in here?
Mr. Stark, are you serious?

We only landed that hit before
because we caught him off guard.

We couldn't find enough of an
opening to finish him off.

If we'd kept fighting, we would
have been the ones killed.
Someone's gotta do this, right?

You're right. Then let's
do our best together.
No, you go to the guard station.
You need to evacuate the townsfolk.
Then you're going to...
Yeah.
I'm going to...

get on my hands and knees
and beg Frieren to return.
What?

Come on! Having her defeat him
is our only option!
I suppose that's more realistic.

The guards will listen to you
if you show them this.
Very well.
I'm heading straight out of town.
What is it?
Your arm is in a terrible state.

Can you pass through the castle gate
looking like that?
I'll be fine. This is normal for a warrior.
Is there something weird about it?

I've never seen a warrior walk
around town with two bloody hands.

You're one to talk. You're
covered in blood, too.
Huh? Whose blood is this?
It's not mine.
Hey! What's the matter with—
Mr. Stark, there's mana in this blood.
Fern!
An axe?
I don't believe it. Am I dreaming?
That was my master's technique.

I'd meant to hit your vitals,
but then you went and moved.
It wasn't my intention to make you suffer.
Why are you surprised?

Is it because I'm standing here when
I supposedly suffered a fatal blow?
Or because you didn't detect our approach?

You aren't the only one who knows how to
conceal her presence by controlling her mana.
Any demon can do it.

That said, it's hardly fitting
for a battle between mages.
You sure like to talk.
Aren't you going to finish me off?

Since I failed to kill you instantly,
I thought I'd ask you some questions.
Or would you rather die right now?
Go ahead.
Is that boy strong?
He's Eisen the Warrior's best student.
I see. How unfortunate.
Poor boy.

He won't die a decent death
at Linie's hands.
One more question.
Where is Frieren?
She fled the town
because you killed the dungeon guard.
Graf Granat said something similar.
Killing a guard is a serious crime, it seems.
The punishment is execution.
Execution?

That wouldn't be enough
to make that woman flee.
She holds a powerful grudge against demons,

enough to teach her own student
a spell purely for demon-killing.
Someone like that wouldn't run.
She must be after something.
It must be Lady Aura.
Don't move.

You know where Ms. Frieren
is headed, don't you?
You're wasting your time.
You lied about failing to kill me.
You wanted revenge for my surprising you.
You're proud and arrogant.

You still don't see us—see anyone
besides Ms. Frieren as a threat.
That's why you granted me an opportunity.

From this distance, I can blast
a hole clean through your heart.
Try it.

Your head will fly before
you get the chance.
Ms. Frieren, am I useful?
Why would you ask that?
I'm not as good at magic as you are.
I've lived for much longer than you.
In that regard, you'll never catch up to me.
I see.
But that only applies to mana and technique.

I often let you handle
battles against monsters.
Yes, you've forced those on me many times.
I'm sorry, okay?
But battles end quicker when you fight

because you fire off spells
faster than I do.

Girl, I have dedicated the majority
of my life to the pursuit of magic.
So have I.
How is she responding so quickly?
If I hadn't reflexively defended myself, that would've pierced my heart.
You blocked it.
So your heart is your weak point.
This girl...
I see.

You weren't lying about
dedicating your life to magic.
Then I shall crush you with all my might.
Balterie.
Sounds like they've begun as well.
It's a shame, though.
We're nearly finished here.
Perhaps I'll observe their battle.
Lord Lügner gets cross when I interfere.
Oh?
We're not finished yet.

You're tough. Perhaps I'll be
able to enjoy this a little.
My mana, technique, and control are all far greater than hers.
This girl cannot compare to me.
However, she's fast.
I'm being overwhelmed by the sheer number of attacks, pure and simple.
Damn you, Frieren. How did you train this girl?
I'll engage her in a battle of attrition and wait for her to exhaust her mana.
No, I can't.
The battle will be over before then.
If I could just create an opening...
Linie, what are you doing?
Hurry up and defeat him!
Honestly, how selfish.

He's refusing to do anything
but fight defensively.
How are you wielding your axe like that?
Those are my master's techniques.
I'm skilled at reading mana.

I memorize the flow of mana
inside a person when they move
and imitate their movements.
Just like this.

I knew it from the first time I saw
your movements at the mansion.

They're the same as those of the
powerful warrior I once memorized.
Coincidences really do happen.
Fate is an interesting thing.
You don't mean...

I am imitating the movements
of Eisen the Warrior.
Seriously? This is crazy.
I can't win this fight.
He finally fell.
I must hurry.
Lord Lügner will be upset with me again.
"Fell"? Have I fallen?
Stand up, Stark.

No matter how battered you get,
you cannot fall.
Yeah, but there's no way I can beat you.
Of course you can't.
I'm stronger than you.
Then...
But you got back up.
That means you haven't lost yet.
What kind of logic is that?

Stark, I'll teach you the secret
to defeating powerful opponents.
It's simple.
Keep getting back up and hitting them.

For warriors, whoever's still standing
at the end is the winner.
Damn it, Master.
You and your weird logic.

I guess your brain's made of muscles,
like the rest of you.
You should've just stayed down.
You already lost.
I'm still standing.
Besides, I remember now.
My master's blows were heavier.
Yours are just imitations after all.

Then I will use those imitations
to send you to your end.
Erfassen.
Balterie!
A wide swing, with no regard for defense.
He's lost his mind.

I was prepared for us to kill each other,
but I shouldn't have been so scared.

Your attacks don't have any
weight behind them at all.
Lightning Strike!
Linie!
Shi—
Zoltraak.
Demon-killing magic...
And you alright
Can you hear me
Trailing along deserted train tracks
Crying excessively
Wanting you to smile
I hold on to memories I'd like to keep fresh
There's something I'd like to tell you
With words more precious than a goodbye
Unremarkable yet special
See, things that couldn't have been
Seen if it weren't for these eyes
Why? They begin to overflow
So, if I were to be born again
I would surely choose this place once more
So, if we were to meet again
I'd never let you go, I'd choose the present
Even if no promises were made
Even if I'm lost in days of loneliness
Those tears will be alright, dawn will surely break
I'm whispering our lullaby
for you to come back home
She has roughly one-fifth of my mana.

I've heard there's a long-lived
mage in these woods.

If she engages her directly,
Frieren will lose.
You are no match for me.
What do you think, Heiter?
It's an elf village.
Kill all the elves.
Because you're a far more powerful mage.
